from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'In our daily life, objects have definite states.', 
            'A light switch is either up or down.', 
            'But atoms follow a different set of rules.', 
            'Quantum objects can exist in multiple states simultaneously.', 
            'This strange "both/and" phenomenon is called superposition.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mystery of Superposition", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Define Classical Side Components
        classical_label = Text("Classical", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(classical_label, "A2")
        
        switch_base = RoundedRectangle(height=1.8, width=1.0, corner_radius=0.1, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(switch_base, "B1", "E3")
        
        toggle = Rectangle(height=0.7, width=0.8, fill_opacity=1, color=GRAY)
        toggle.move_to(switch_base.get_center() + UP * 0.4)
        
        on_label = Text("ON", font_size=18, color=GREEN)
        off_label = Text("OFF", font_size=18, color=RED)
        on_label.next_to(switch_base, UP, buff=0.1)
        off_label.next_to(switch_base, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        classical_group = VGroup(classical_label, switch_base, toggle, on_label, off_label)
        self.play(FadeIn(classical_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Rapid clicking to show definite states
        for _ in range(2):
            self.play(toggle.animate.move_to(switch_base.get_center() + DOWN * 0.4), run_time=0.4)
            self.play(toggle.animate.move_to(switch_base.get_center() + UP * 0.4), run_time=0.4)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Introduce Quantum side
        quantum_label = Text("Quantum", color="#00FFFF", font_size=24)
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_label, "A5")
        
        # The glowing sphere
        quantum_sphere = Circle(radius=0.8, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.4)
        glow_layer = Circle(radius=1.1, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.15, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_in_area(quantum_sphere, "B4", "E6")
        self.place_in_area(glow_layer, "B4", "E6")
        
        quantum_group = VGroup(quantum_label, quantum_sphere, glow_layer)
        self.play(FadeIn(quantum_group))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pulsating energy effect
        self.play(
            quantum_sphere.animate.scale(1.2).set_opacity(0.6),
            glow_layer.animate.scale(1.3).set_opacity(0.05),
            rate_func=there_and_back,
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Reveal overlapping states
        # State UP
        s_up_base = RoundedRectangle(height=1.2, width=0.7, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.2)
        s_up_toggle = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.5, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        s_up_toggle.move_to(s_up_base.get_center() + UP * 0.3)
        s_up = VGroup(s_up_base, s_up_toggle)
        
        # State DOWN
        s_down_base = RoundedRectangle(height=1.2, width=0.7, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.2)
        s_down_toggle = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.5, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        s_down_toggle.move_to(s_down_base.get_center() + DOWN * 0.3)
        s_down = VGroup(s_down_base, s_down_toggle)
        
        label_up = Text("UP", font_size=16, color="#FF00FF")
        label_down = Text("DOWN", font_size=16, color="#FF00FF")
        
        # Position them inside the quantum sphere area
        self.place_in_area(s_up, "C4", "E6")
        self.place_in_area(s_down, "C4", "E6")
        label_up.next_to(s_up, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_down.next_to(s_down, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        superposition_states = VGroup(s_up, s_down, label_up, label_down)
        
        # Transition: Sphere dims, states appear
        self.play(
            quantum_sphere.animate.set_opacity(0.1),
            glow_layer.animate.set_opacity(0.02),
            FadeIn(superposition_states)
        )
        
        # Final emphasis
        self.play(Indicate(superposition_states, color="#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize Scene
        title = "Prerequisite: The Language of Vectors"
        lines = [
            "Physicists use arrows, or vectors, to represent states.",
            "Vertical is State A; horizontal is State B.",
            "A diagonal arrow represents a mixture of both."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Positions from Grid
        origin_pt = self.grid["E2"]
        state_a_pt = self.grid["B2"]
        state_b_pt = self.grid["E5"]
        super_pt = self.grid["B5"]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Physicists use arrows, or vectors, to represent states.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Basis Vectors
        arrow_a = Arrow(origin_pt, state_a_pt, color="#00FF00", buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        arrow_b = Arrow(origin_pt, state_b_pt, color="#FFFF00", buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(arrow_a),
            GrowArrow(arrow_b),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Vertical is State A; horizontal is State B.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting State definitions
        
        # Labels for Basis Vectors using Unicode for Braket notation
        label_a = Text("|0⟩", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        label_b = Text("|1⟩", font_size=24, color="#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "E6")
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(label_a),
            FadeIn(label_b),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # A diagonal arrow represents a mixture of both.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Superposition Vector
        arrow_psi = Arrow(origin_pt, super_pt, color="#FFFFFF", buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        label_psi = Text("|ψ⟩", font_size=28, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(label_psi, "A5")
        
        # Projection lines
        proj_h = DashedLine(super_pt, [origin_pt[0], super_pt[1], 0], color="#888888")
        proj_v = DashedLine(super_pt, [super_pt[0], origin_pt[1], 0], color="#888888")
        
        self.play(
            GrowArrow(arrow_psi),

            run_time=1.5

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            'We define the quantum state with this equation.',
            "Alpha and beta tell us the state's composition.",
            'Think of mixing blue and red paint together.',
            'Purple paint represents the superposition state psi.',
            'These coefficients determine the strength of each component.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Superposition State", lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_0 = "#00FFFF"  # Blue/Cyan
        COLOR_1 = "#FF00FF"  # Red/Magenta
        COLOR_PSI = "#A020F0" # Purple

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Formula: |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩ using Text/Unicode symbols
        f_psi = Text("|ψ⟩")
        f_eq = Text(" = ")
        f_alpha = Text("α", color=COLOR_0)
        f_ket0 = Text("|0⟩")
        f_plus = Text(" + ")
        f_beta = Text("β", color=COLOR_1)
        f_ket1 = Text("|1⟩")
        
        formula = VGroup(f_psi, f_eq, f_alpha, f_ket0, f_plus, f_beta, f_ket1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight alpha and beta
        self.play(
            f_alpha.animate.scale(1.2),
            f_beta.animate.scale(1.2),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            f_alpha.animate.scale(1/1.2),
            f_beta.animate.scale(1/1.2),
            run_time=0.5
        )

        # Create Beaker
        beaker_outline = VGroup(
            Line([-0.7, 0.8, 0], [-0.7, -0.8, 0]), 
            Line([-0.7, -0.8, 0], [0.7, -0.8, 0]),  
            Line([0.7, -0.8, 0], [0.7, 0.8, 0]),    
        ).set_stroke(WHITE, width=4)
        
        beaker_label = Text("|ψ⟩", font_size=24)
        beaker_group = VGroup(beaker_outline, beaker_label)
        self.place_in_area(beaker_group, "C3", "E4", scale_factor=1.0)
        beaker_label.next_to(beaker_outline, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(beaker_outline), FadeIn(beaker_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Blue pour stream
        blue_stream = Rectangle(width=0.08, height=1.2, color=COLOR_0, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_at_grid(blue_stream, "B3")
        blue_stream.shift(DOWN * 0.3)
        
        # Blue liquid filling
        blue_liquid = Rectangle(width=1.3, height=0.01, color=COLOR_0, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        blue_liquid.move_to(beaker_outline[1].get_center() + UP * 0.05)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(blue_stream, shift=DOWN))
        self.play(
            blue_liquid.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.6).shift(UP * 0.3),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(blue_stream))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Red pour stream
        red_stream = Rectangle(width=0.08, height=1.2, color=COLOR_1, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        self.place_at_grid(red_stream, "B4")
        red_stream.shift(DOWN * 0.3)
        
        # Red liquid filling
        red_liquid = Rectangle(width=1.3, height=0.01, color=COLOR_1, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        red_liquid.move_to(blue_liquid.get_top() + UP * 0.01)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(red_stream, shift=DOWN))
        self.play(
            red_liquid.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.6).shift(UP * 0.3),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(FadeOut(red_stream))
        
        # Mix to Purple
        mixed_liquid = Rectangle(width=1.3, height=1.2, color=COLOR_PSI, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        mixed_liquid.move_to(beaker_outline[1].get_center() + UP * 0.6)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(VGroup(blue_liquid, red_liquid), mixed_liquid),
            beaker_label.animate.set_color(COLOR_PSI),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pulse coefficients for emphasis
        self.play(
            f_alpha.animate.scale(1.4).set_color(WHITE),
            f_beta.animate.scale(1.4).set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=0.4,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        self.play(
            f_alpha.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(COLOR_0),
            f_beta.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(COLOR_1),
            run_time=0.4,
            rate_func=there_and_back
        )
        
        self.wait(2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(WHITE)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title = "The Math of Probability (Born's Rule)"
        lines = [
            "Squaring the coefficients reveals the real-world odds.",
            "The total probability must always equal one hundred percent.",
            "Even odds mean a fifty-fifty chance for either state."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_ALPHA = "#00FFFF"  # Cyan
        COLOR_BETA = "#FF00FF"   # Magenta
        COLOR_GREEN = "#00FF00"
        COLOR_GOLD = "#FFD700"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_ALPHA))
        
        # Equation: |α|² + |β|² = 1
        # Using separate Text objects for individual coloring
        eq_alpha = Text("|α|²", color=COLOR_ALPHA)
        eq_plus = Text(" + ", color=WHITE)
        eq_beta = Text("|β|²", color=COLOR_BETA)
        eq_equals = Text(" = 1", color=WHITE)
        equation = VGroup(eq_alpha, eq_plus, eq_beta, eq_equals).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(equation, "A2", "A5", scale_factor=1.0)

        label_a = Text("Prob(0)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_ALPHA)
        label_b = Text("Prob(1)", font_size=20, color=COLOR_BETA)
        self.place_at_grid(label_a, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_b, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(FadeIn(equation), FadeIn(label_a), FadeIn(label_b))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Chameleon representation: A rounded rectangle with eyes
        body = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.3, height=0.8, width=1.2, fill_opacity=1)
        eye_l = Circle(radius=0.08, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).shift(LEFT*0.2 + UP*0.1)
        eye_r = Circle(radius=0.08, color=BLACK, fill_opacity=1).shift(RIGHT*0.2 + UP*0.1)
        chameleon = VGroup(body, eye_l, eye_r)
        self.place_at_grid(chameleon, "D2", scale_factor=1.2)

        self.play(FadeIn(chameleon))
        
        # Rapidly shifting color
        for _ in range(4):
            self.play(body.animate.set_color(COLOR_GREEN), run_time=0.2)
            self.play(body.animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD), run_time=0.2)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD))

        # Bar Chart
        # Initial 50/50 bars
        bar_width = 0.6
        max_height = 2.0
        
        green_bar = Rectangle(width=bar_width, height=max_height * 0.5, color=COLOR_GREEN, fill_opacity=0.8)
        gold_bar = Rectangle(width=bar_width, height=max_height * 0.5, color=COLOR_GOLD, fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        # Grid positions for bars
        self.place_at_grid(green_bar, "F4")
        self.place_at_grid(gold_bar, "F5")
        # Adjusting alignment so they grow from bottom
        green_bar.align_to(self.grid["F4"], DOWN)
        gold_bar.align_to(self.grid["F5"], DOWN)

        label_green = Text("Green", font_size=18, color=COLOR_GREEN)
        label_gold = Text("Gold", font_size=18, color=COLOR_GOLD)
        self.place_at_grid(label_green, "E4", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(label_gold, "E5", scale_factor=0.8)

        self.play(GrowFromEdge(green_bar, DOWN), GrowFromEdge(gold_bar, DOWN), FadeIn(label_green), FadeIn(label_gold))
        self.wait(1)

        # Animate changing heights to 70% and 30%
        # Calculate new centers after resizing from bottom
        new_green_height = max_height * 0.7
        new_gold_height = max_height * 0.3
        
        self.play(
            green_bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(new_green_height).align_to(self.grid["F4"], DOWN),
            gold_bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(new_gold_height).align_to(self.grid["F5"], DOWN),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Flash MEASURE
        measure_flash = Text("MEASURE!", color=RED, weight=BOLD)
        self.place_in_area(measure_flash, "C3", "D5", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(measure_flash))
        self.play(Flash(measure_flash, color=RED, line_length=0.4))
        self.play(FadeOut(measure_flash))

        # Final collapse to Gold
        self.play(
            body.animate.set_color(COLOR_GOLD),
            gold_bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(max_height).align_to(self.grid["F5"], DOWN),
            green_bar.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(0.01).align_to(self.grid["F4"], DOWN),
            FadeOut(green_bar),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(2)
from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lines
        title_str = "The Measurement Act: Wavefunction Collapse"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Superposition lasts only until we take a look.',
            'Measuring forces the system to choose one reality.',
            'The blurry wave suddenly collapses into a single point.',
            'Before opening the box, the cat is both states.',
            'Observation turns quantum mystery into classical fact.'
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # Helper to create a stylized cat silhouette
        def create_cat_silhouette(color, label_text):
            body = Ellipse(width=0.5, height=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            head = Circle(radius=0.18, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to(body.get_left() + UP*0.1)
            ear1 = Triangle(color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.06).move_to(head.get_top() + LEFT*0.06 + UP*0.03)
            ear2 = Triangle(color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).scale(0.06).move_to(head.get_top() + RIGHT*0.06 + UP*0.03)
            label = Text(label_text, font_size=18, color=color)
            cat = VGroup(body, head, ear1, ear2)
            label.next_to(cat, DOWN, buff=0.1)
            return VGroup(cat, label)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Render a blurry, spread-out cyan wave (#00FFFF)
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Create a "wavefunction" made of multiple overlapping sine waves
        wave_group = VGroup()
        for i in range(8):
            wave_layer = FunctionGraph(
                lambda x: 0.5 * np.sin(1.2 * x + i * 0.3),
                x_range=[-2, 2],
                color="#00FFFF",
                stroke_opacity=0.25
            )
            wave_group.add(wave_layer)
        
        self.place_in_area(wave_group, "B2", "E5")
        self.play(Create(wave_group), run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display two cat silhouettes as translucent overlays: one 'Sleeping' (#888888) and one 'Awake' (#FFFFFF)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#888888"))
        
        sleeping_cat = create_cat_silhouette("#888888", "Sleeping").set_opacity(0.4)
        awake_cat = create_cat_silhouette("#FFFFFF", "Awake").set_opacity(0.4)
        
        self.place_at_grid(sleeping_cat, "C3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(awake_cat, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(sleeping_cat), FadeIn(awake_cat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # An eye icon representing an 'Observer' (#FFFF00) appears and looks toward the center.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        eye_outer = Ellipse(width=0.7, height=0.35, color="#FFFF00", stroke_width=3)
        eye_iris = Dot(color="#FFFF00", radius=0.12)
        observer = VGroup(eye_outer, eye_iris)
        self.place_at_grid(observer, "B5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(observer, shift=LEFT))
        # Look toward the center
        self.play(eye_iris.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.15), run_time=1)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # The spread-out wave instantly collapses into a single, sharp vertical white line (#FFFFFF).
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        center_pos = self.grid["D3"]
        sharp_line = Line(
            center_pos + UP * 0.7,
            center_pos + DOWN * 0.7,
            color="#FFFFFF",
            stroke_width=5
        )
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(wave_group, sharp_line),
            run_time=0.5,
            rate_func=exponential_decay
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The 'Sleeping' cat silhouette fades away completely, while 'Awake' cat becomes solid and fully opaque.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(sleeping_cat),
            awake_cat.animate.set_opacity(1.0).scale(1.3).move_to(self.grid["C4"]),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_str = "Application: Why Superposition Powers the Future"
        lines = [
            "Superposition allows computers to process data in parallel.",
            "A quantum mouse explores every path at once.",
            "This massive speedup will transform our digital future."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)
        
        # Reference for grid dictionary
        G = self.grid

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Draw Maze Walls
        # Outer Boundary (A1 to F6)
        # Offset boundaries to create the "box" around grid points
        boundary = VGroup(
            Line(G["A1"] + UL*0.45, G["A6"] + UR*0.45), # Top
            Line(G["A6"] + UR*0.45, G["F6"] + DR*0.45), # Right
            Line(G["F6"] + DR*0.45, G["F1"] + DL*0.45), # Bottom
            Line(G["F1"] + DL*0.45, G["A1"] + UL*0.45)  # Left
        ).set_color(GRAY_C).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        # Internal Obstacles
        int_walls = VGroup(
            Line(G["B1"] + DL*0.45, G["B5"] + DR*0.45), # Horizontal barrier
            Line(G["A2"] + UR*0.45, G["D2"] + DR*0.45), # Vertical barrier
            Line(G["D4"] + UL*0.45, G["D6"] + UR*0.45)  # Another horizontal
        ).set_color(GRAY_C).set_stroke(width=4)
        
        maze = VGroup(boundary, int_walls)
        
        start_label = Text("START", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(G["A1"], LEFT, buff=0.3)
        exit_label = Text("EXIT", font_size=16, color=WHITE).next_to(G["F6"], RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        self.play(Create(maze), FadeIn(start_label), FadeIn(exit_label))
        
        # Classical Mouse (White Dot)
        classical_mouse = Dot(color="#FFFFFF", radius=0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(classical_mouse, "A1")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(classical_mouse))
        
        # Simulation: Try one path, fail, backtrack
        self.play(classical_mouse.animate.move_to(G["A2"]), run_time=0.6)
        self.play(classical_mouse.animate.scale(1.2).set_color(RED), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(classical_mouse.animate.scale(1/1.2).set_color(WHITE), run_time=0.1)
        self.play(classical_mouse.animate.move_to(G["A1"]), run_time=0.6)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Using hex for Cyan to ensure compatibility
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Quantum Mouse (Cyan Dot)
        quantum_mouse_start = Dot(color="#00FFFF", radius=0.15)
        self.place_at_grid(quantum_mouse_start, "A1")
        
        self.play(FadeOut(classical_mouse), FadeIn(quantum_mouse_start))
        
        # Split into superposition (Parallel paths)
        q_copy1 = quantum_mouse_start.copy() # Path A
        q_copy2 = quantum_mouse_start.copy() # Path B
        q_copy3 = quantum_mouse_start.copy() # Success path
        
        self.add(q_copy1, q_copy2, q_copy3)
        self.remove(quantum_mouse_start)
        
        # Simultaneous exploration
        self.play(
            q_copy1.animate.move_to(G["A2"]),
            q_copy2.animate.move_to(G["B4"]),
            q_copy3.animate.move_to(G["B1"]),
            run_time=1.2
        )
        
        self.play(
            q_copy3.animate.move_to(G["F1"]),
            run_time=1.0
        )
        
        self.play(
            q_copy3.animate.move_to(G["F6"]),
            run_time=1.0
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Exit found!
        success_flash = Circle(radius=0.2, color="#FFFF00").move_to(G["F6"])
        
        self.play(
            q_copy3.animate.set_color("#FFFF00").scale(1.8),
            FadeIn(success_flash),
            q_copy1.animate.set_opacity(0),
            q_copy2.animate.set_opacity(0),
        )
        
        self.play(
            success_flash.animate.scale(3).set_opacity(0),
            run_time=0.8
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Mystery of Superposition: How Quantum Objects Do Two Things at Once
outline.target_audience: High school seniors or first-year university students with basic algebra knowledge

sections.title: The Intuition Gap: Classical vs. Quantum
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental difference between the 'Either/Or' world we see and the 'Both/And' world of atoms. Use a high-paced animation to show a classical object (a light switch) compared to a quantum object.
sections.example: A standard light switch is either 'On' or 'Off'. A 'Quantum Switch' exists in a blurry, glowing state of being both flicked up and down simultaneously until you touch it.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Vectors
sections.content: Explain that in physics, states are represented by arrows (vectors). To understand superposition, we must view states as directions in space. If 'Up' is State A and 'Right' is State B, a diagonal arrow is a mix of both.
sections.example: Visualize a compass needle. North is |0⟩ and East is |1⟩. A needle pointing North-East is a vector sum of both directions, representing a state that isn't purely North or purely East.

sections.title: Defining the Superposition State
sections.content: Introduce the state vector equation |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩. Explain that α and β are 'probability amplitudes' (coefficients) that determine how much of each state is present. Use a color-mixing animation to represent this.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Quantum Paint Bucket' containing a mix of 70% Blue (|0⟩) and 30% Red (|1⟩). The resulting Purple liquid is the superposition state |ψ⟩.

sections.title: The Math of Probability (Born's Rule)
sections.content: Translate the abstract vector into real-world odds. Use a bar chart that transforms into a wave height graph. Explain that the square of the coefficients (|α|² and |β|²) must equal 1 (100% total probability).
sections.example: If α is 0.707 (1/√2), then |α|² is 0.5. This means when we check our 'Quantum Chameleon,' there is a 50% chance it turns Green and a 50% chance it turns Gold.

sections.title: The Measurement Act: Wavefunction Collapse
sections.content: Explain that the act of 'looking' (measurement) forces the universe to choose one state. Graphically show a spread-out wave suddenly spiking into a single point. This is the transition from quantum to classical reality.
sections.example: Schrödinger’s Cat: Inside a box, the cat is represented by a ghost-like overlay of 'Sleeping' and 'Awake'. The moment the lid is opened (measurement), the overlay disappears, leaving only one physical cat.

sections.title: Application: Why Superposition Powers the Future
sections.content: Conclude by showing how superposition allows quantum computers to process massive amounts of data in parallel, unlike classical bits that work one-by-one.
sections.example: A classical mouse in a maze must try every path one after another. A 'Quantum Mouse' uses superposition to explore every possible path at the exact same time, finding the exit instantly.

storyboard.title: The Intuition Gap: Classical vs. Quantum
lecture_lines: In our daily life, objects have definite states.
A light switch is either up or down.
But atoms follow a different set of rules.
Quantum objects can exist in multiple states simultaneously.
This strange "both/and" phenomenon is called superposition.

The classical switch [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/switch.svg] toggles between 'ON' and 'OFF' (#FFFFFF) to show definite states.
A glowing, blurry sphere appears on the right, labeled 'Quantum' (#00FFFF), pulsating with cyan energy.
The sphere reveals two translucent switches [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/switch.svg], 'UP' and 'DOWN' (#FF00FF), existing simultaneously in the same space.
The label 'SUPERPOSITION' (#00FFFF) flashes above the sphere as it pulses rapidly.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Vectors
lecture_lines: Physicists use arrows, or vectors, to represent states.
Vertical is State A; horizontal is State B.
A diagonal arrow represents a mixture of both.
animations: Display a vertical arrow labeled '|0⟩' (#00FF00) and a horizontal arrow labeled '|1⟩' (#FFFF00) starting from a single point.
Draw a diagonal arrow labeled '|ψ⟩' (#FFFFFF) emerging from the same origin, pointing between the two directions.
Show dashed lines (#888888) projecting from the tip of '|ψ⟩' to the '|0⟩' and '|1⟩' arrows to visualize component parts.

storyboard.title: Defining the Superposition State
lecture_lines: We define the quantum state with this equation.
Alpha and beta tell us the state's composition.
Think of mixing blue and red paint together.
Purple paint represents the superposition state psi.
These coefficients determine the strength of each component.
animations: Display the formula '|ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩' at the top, with α colored #00FFFF and β colored #FF00FF.
A central beaker [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beaker.svg] labeled '|ψ⟩' appears on the screen.
A blue liquid stream (#00FFFF) representing '|0⟩' pours into the beaker [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beaker.svg].
A red liquid stream (#FF00FF) representing '|1⟩' is added to the same beaker [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/beaker.svg].
The liquids mix into a purple color (#A020F0), and the coefficients α and β pulse to indicate the mix ratio.

storyboard.title: The Math of Probability (Born's Rule)
lecture_lines: Squaring the coefficients reveals the real-world odds.
This shifting chameleon represents our uncertain quantum state.
Probabilities often start balanced at fifty-fifty.
But these chances can vary based on the coefficients.
Measuring forces one outcome with one hundred percent certainty.
animations: Show the equation '|α|² + |β|² = 1' with |α|² labeled 'Prob(0)' (#00FFFF) and |β|² labeled 'Prob(1)' (#FF00FF).
A bar chart with 'Green' (#00FF00) and 'Gold' (#FFD700) bars appears, showing their combined total is constant.
The bars equalize at 50% height each to represent even odds, while a chameleon icon [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ch.svg] flashes between the two colors.
